violation_type.title: Child Passenger Safety Seat System - Secure Each Child in Appropriate System According to Manufacturer's Instructions (26 TAC §746.5607(c))
violation_type.short_title: Child Passenger Safety Seat System - Secure Each Child in Appropriate System According to Manufacturer's Instructions
violation_type.typical_finding: Booster seats were not being utilized for children with a height of 4 feet, 8 inches or less as required by standards.

finding_variants.text: Booster seats were not being utilized for children with a height of 4 feet, 8 inches or less as required by standards.

Based on the investigation findings, this standard was reviewed and found to be in non-compliance with The Minimum Standards for Child Care Centers. The operation transported two three-year-old children; the operation only had one forward facing child safety seat on the vehicle available for use. The operation staff did not know the weights or heights of any the fifteen children ages 4 through 7 years old that were transported; the operation could not determine if these children required more than a safety belt.
During this investigation it has been determined that the operation has violated the standard for children 12 years old and under riding in the front seat.
Booster seats are not being used when transporting children ages 4-6 years old.

The operation has two transportation vehicles that need repairs to their seatbelt. The first vehicle was missing the safety latch for the seat belt to go into for safety. The second vehicle did not have the safety latch to place the seat belt inside once a child was in the seat.
